question: What is the primary goal of decontamination in a clinical setting?

options.A: To completely eliminate all moisture from equipment
options.B: To reduce the financial cost of hospital supplies
options.C: To make medical instruments look shiny and new
options.D: To remove or destroy harmful microorganisms

explanation: Decontamination focuses specifically on eliminating pathogens to render items safe for clinical use. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h1)

question: A patient develops a new infection due to poorly cleaned surgical tools. This failure highlights a breakdown in which process?
explanation: Failing to properly process instruments allows microorganisms to transfer to patients, causing hospital-acquired infections. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h1)

question: Which decontamination level is capable of destroying bacterial spores?
explanation: Sterilization is the only process among the choices that completely destroys all microbial life, including spores. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h2)

question: Why must a nurse wash organic matter off an instrument before applying a chemical disinfectant?

options.A: Cleaning raises the room temperature for faster drying
options.B: Dirt and blood can shield microorganisms from the disinfectant
options.C: Detergents enhance the expiry date of chemical solutions
options.D: Organic material turns the metal instruments completely black

explanation: Residual organic matter inactivates chemical agents and prevents direct contact with underlying pathogens. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h2)

question: An item that enters sterile body tissues or the vascular system is classified as what?
explanation: Critical items carry a high risk of infection if contaminated and must be sterile. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h3)

question: A nurse prepares a stethoscope for use on a stable patient. According to Spaulding, how should this item be processed?

options.A: Low-level disinfection because it only touches intact skin
options.B: High-level disinfection because it enters the respiratory tract
options.C: Absolute sterilization because it belongs to a patient
options.D: Incineration because it cannot be wiped down safely

explanation: Stethoscopes touch intact skin only, placing them in the non-critical category requiring simple wiping. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h3)

question: What is the very first action a nurse should take with an instrument immediately after a procedure?

options.A: Place it directly into a sterilizing autoclave
options.B: Store it back inside the sterile instrument drawer
options.C: Submerge it in concentrated bleach for one hour
options.D: Wipe off gross soil and keep it moist

explanation: Removing gross debris right away stops organic material from drying onto the surface. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h4)

question: Why must washed instruments be completely dried before undergoing sterilization?

options.A: Water droplets react with air to create toxic gases
options.B: Wet instruments make the autoclave cycle run much faster
options.C: Moisture can dilute chemical agents and cause rusting
options.D: Dry metal conducts electricity better during the process

explanation: Excess water interferes with sterilization efficacy and damages metallic instruments through corrosion. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h4)

question: What happens to chlorine disinfectant solutions when they are exposed to heat and light over time?

options.A: They turn into safe drinking water
options.B: They degrade rapidly and lose their potency
options.C: They become completely sterile on their own
options.D: They transform into high-level liquid soap

explanation: Chlorine solutions are unstable and break down quickly, which is why fresh batches must be prepared regularly. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h5)

question: Why is 'contact time' a critical factor when wiping a treatment table with a chemical disinfectant?

options.A: The chemical needs enough time to kill the microorganisms present
options.B: It allows the chemical smell to fully dissipate from the room
options.C: It gives the nurse time to finish charting patient notes
options.D: Longer drying times prevent the paint from peeling off

explanation: Disinfectants do not work instantly; they require a specific duration of wet contact to destroy pathogens. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h5)

question: Which PPE item is best suited for washing sharp surgical instruments in the utility room?
explanation: Utility gloves provide puncture and chemical resistance that thin examination gloves lack. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h6)

question: What is the immediate action required if a chemical disinfectant accidentally splashes into a nurse's eye?

options.A: Rub the eye vigorously to spread the chemical evenly
options.B: Cover the affected eye tightly with a clean gauze pad
options.C: Flush the eye with clean water for at least fifteen minutes
options.D: Wait until the end of the shift to report the incident

explanation: Immediate and prolonged water irrigation minimizes chemical injury to ocular tissues. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h6)

question: What is the primary risk of overfilling a sharp disposal container in a ward?

options.A: The plastic container changing its official color
options.B: Unpleasant odors spreading down the hallway
options.C: An increase in general municipal water bills

explanation: Overfilled sharp boxes expose nurses and cleaners to protruding needles and blades. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h7)

question: When cleaning up a large blood spill on a ward floor, what is the correct wiping motion?

options.A: From the outer edges inward to contain the spill
options.B: A random circular motion across the entire floor
options.C: Leaving the blood to dry before sweeping it away
options.D: From the center outward to spread the fluid quickly

explanation: Working from the periphery inward prevents the contamination from spreading across a wider floor area. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h7)
